seo_about_body: Dofus Forge is a free online build planner for Dofus 3. Equip items from the complete catalog, track set bonuses in real time, simulate Magesmithy (Forgemagie) runes, and let the stat optimizer find the best gear combination for your character — no account or installation needed.
seo_feature_catalog_desc: Browse every Dofus 3 item by slot, level, element and set, with real in-game icons and stats.
seo_feature_sets_desc: See active set bonuses update live as you equip pieces from the same Dofus set.
seo_feature_runes_desc: Simulate Forgemagie rune slots and their stat bonuses before spending resources in-game.
seo_feature_optimizer_desc: The Forger auto-generates the best equipment combination for your target stats and constraints.
seo_feature_share_desc: Every build gets a unique URL — share your setup instantly, no login required.
seo_feature_explore_desc: Browse, bookmark and rate builds published by other players.
seo_how_2: Equip items slot by slot from the catalog.
seo_how_3: Watch your stats and set bonuses update in real time.
seo_how_4: Share your build link or publish it to Explore.
seo_faq_a1: Yes, it's completely free and no account is required to build or share.
seo_faq_q2: Does it support all Dofus classes?
seo_faq_a2: Yes, every current Dofus 3 class is supported with its spells and characteristics.
seo_faq_q3: Is the item data up to date?
seo_faq_a3: Yes, item and set data is kept in sync with the current Dofus 3 game version.
seo_faq_q4: Can I share my build with others?
seo_faq_a4: Yes, every build generates a unique shareable URL instantly.
seo_faq_q5: Is Dofus Forge available in my language?
seo_faq_a5: Dofus Forge is available in English, Spanish, French and Portuguese.
explore_seo_description: Browse Dofus 3 builds shared by the community — filter by class, sort by rating, likes or views, and find inspiration for your own setup.

seo_classes_body: Build for any class — Iop, Cra, Eniripsa, Sram, Sacrier, Sadida and every other Dofus 3 class, each with its own spells, characteristics and best-in-slot gear.
about_seo_description: Dofus Forge is a free, fan-made build planner for Dofus 3. Learn why it exists, where its data comes from, and who makes it.
about_intro: Dofus Forge is a free, fan-made build planner for Dofus 3 — a tool built by a player, for players, to make planning gear and stats less tedious than testing everything live in-game.
about_why_body: Testing gear combinations in Dofus costs kamas, forgemagie dust and time. Dofus Forge lets you try any item, any set, any rune combination instantly, see the resulting stats and set bonuses right away, and only commit once you like the numbers.
about_data_body: Item, set and spell data comes from the DofusDude API and is kept in sync with the current Dofus 3 game version shown in the header. Nothing is hand-entered or guessed.
about_free_body: Building and sharing a setup is free and doesn't require an account. Signing in is optional — it unlocks saving builds to the cloud, publishing them to Explore, and liking, rating or commenting on other players' builds.
about_team_body: Built and maintained by Juan (Wembie). Game data and testing happen on the Tal Kasha server, with in-game support from Raik-Luck.
howto_seo_description: A step-by-step guide to planning a Dofus 3 build — picking a class, equipping items, reading stats and set bonuses, forgemagie runes, the stat optimizer, and sharing your build.
howto_intro: No sign-up needed to start — open the planner and follow along. Here's every step, in order.
howto_step1_body: Choose your class from the Class panel and set your level — characteristic points to allocate update automatically based on it.
howto_step2_body: Click any empty slot in the Equipment grid to open the catalog. Filter by level, element, set or stat, then click an item to equip it.
howto_step3_body: The Stats panel recalculates live as you equip gear or allocate points. Active Set Bonuses appear automatically once you have 2 or more pieces from the same set.
howto_step4_body: Click an equipped item to add runes and simulate their stat bonuses before spending real resources in-game.
howto_step5_title: 5. Let the optimizer find the best gear
howto_step5_body: "The Forger" auto-generates the best equipment combination for a stat you target, given your constraints — open it from the header.
howto_step6_body: Toggle Compare to see your current build side by side against another one, stat by stat.
howto_step7_body: Share copies a link to your exact setup instantly, no account needed. Sign in to Publish it to Explore so other players can find, rate and comment on it.
howto_step8_body: My Builds lists everything you've saved, with visibility controls — private, unlisted, or public.

privacy_intro: This Privacy and Personal Data Processing Policy explains which personal data Dofus Forge processes when you visit dofusforge.com or use your account, why, who it is shared with and how to exercise your rights. It complies with Colombian Law 1581 of 2012 and its regulations and, where they apply to you, the EU and UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), Brazil's General Data Protection Law (LGPD) and United States privacy laws.
privacy_s1_body:
The controller of your personal data is Juan Acosta, the independent developer who operates Dofus Forge from Colombia. For any privacy matter, including exercising your rights, write to contact@dofusforge.com.
Dofus Forge is an independent fan project: it is not affiliated with Ankama, and Ankama receives no data from this site.
privacy_s2_body:

• Content and activity: builds (public, unlisted or private) and their version history, collections, comments, likes, ratings, bookmarks, followers and follows, reports you submit and notifications.
• Technical data: IP address, browser, device and requested pages, which our providers process to deliver the site and protect it from abuse. To count build views and optimizer runs without duplicates we store a pseudonymous identifier (a hash) derived from your IP; we never store the IP itself.
• Data on your device: language, theme, sound, interface settings and build drafts are kept in your browser's local storage and never reach our servers unless you save a build to your account.
We do not ask for or process sensitive data, identity documents or payment data.
privacy_s3_title: Why we use your data and on what legal basis
privacy_s3_body:
• Providing the service and managing your account (sign-up, sign-in, saving and displaying your content, notifications, and confirmation or password-reset emails): performance of the contract you accept with the Terms.
• Security, spam prevention and moderation (bot verification, rate limits, reports): our legitimate interest in keeping the site safe.
• Aggregate statistics (build views, optimizer usage and Cloudflare Web Analytics, which uses no cookies): our legitimate interest in understanding and improving the site.
• Measurement with Google Analytics (pages visited and actions such as equipping items, running the optimizer, or publishing and sharing builds): your consent in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland, and our legitimate interest in understanding and improving the site elsewhere.
• Advertising: personalized ads only with your consent where the law requires it; without it, Google may show non-personalized or limited ads.
• Complying with legal obligations and requests from authorities: legal obligation.
In Colombia, ticking this Policy's box gives us your prior, express and informed authorization to process your data for these purposes (Law 1581 of 2012, art. 9). In Brazil the equivalent bases of LGPD art. 7 apply. We send no marketing emails and make no automated decisions that produce legal effects on you.
privacy_s4_body:
We do not sell or rent your personal data. Only the following have access to it:
• Other users and the public: your profile (username, display name, avatar, bio, followers and public builds) and the content you make public. Unlisted content is visible to anyone with the link; private content is not shown to other users.
• Supabase Inc. (USA): database, authentication, file storage and account emails.
• Cloudflare Inc. (USA): hosting, content delivery, attack protection, Turnstile bot verification, Web Analytics and image storage.
• Google LLC and Google Ireland Ltd.: Google AdSense advertising, measurement with Google Analytics (loaded through Google Tag Manager) and Google Fonts typefaces. All of them are downloaded from Google's servers, which therefore receive your IP.
• Authorities, when a law or a valid order requires it, or to defend our rights against a claim.
Supabase, Cloudflare and Google, for Google Analytics, act as processors: they may only use the data to provide their service to us, under their data protection agreements. Google also acts as an independent controller for its own advertising.
privacy_s5_body: Our providers may store or process your data outside your country, mainly in the United States. These transfers rely on the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses or on each provider's EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification, as applicable, and, for Colombia, on your authorization and art. 26 of Law 1581 of 2012. By accepting this Policy you authorize that transfer and transmission.
privacy_s6_body:

The site cannot work without them, so they do not require consent.

You can delete or block cookies and local storage in your browser; if you block the necessary ones, signing in stops working.

forgeguide_seo_title: The Forger guide — Dofus 3 build optimizer | Dofus Forge
forgeguide_seo_description: How to use Dofus Forge's build optimizer, The Forger: minimums, purity and caps, intensity, pinned and banned items, forgemagic, transcendence runes and exos, and how to read the results.
forgeguide_intro: You place an order — "11 AP, 6 MP, 40% resistance everywhere, and as much Strength as possible" — and The Forger tries millions of gear combinations in your browser until it finds the one that fits it best, with characteristic points, forgemagic and set bonuses already worked out. This guide covers every part of it, from your first forge to tricks for hard orders.
forgeguide_start_intro: The bare minimum to get a useful build in under a minute.
forgeguide_start_1_body: In the planner. The Forger never suggests items above your character's level.
forgeguide_start_2_body: With its button in the planner's top bar (on a phone, from the menu) or with the button at the top of this guide.
forgeguide_start_3_body: Tap a stat to turn it on and set its minimum (e.g. AP ≥ 11, MP ≥ 6). Also turn on the ones you want as high as possible, even without a minimum.
forgeguide_start_4_body: Standard intensity is enough for almost everything. The Forger tempers itself once the piece stops improving.
forgeguide_start_5_body: "Load this build" sends it to the planner with items, runes and points. Ctrl+Z undoes it like any other change.
forgeguide_order_title: The order: minimum, purity and cap
forgeguide_order_intro: Every active stat has three values. With them you say what is mandatory, how much each point is worth and how far it is worth going.
forgeguide_order_1_body: What the piece must have, no matter what. The Forger meets every minimum first; a build that misses one always ranks below one that meets them all.
forgeguide_order_2_body: What each point of that stat is worth. Points missing from the minimum cost their purity and surplus points earn it. The 5 diamonds are shortcuts (from ×¼ to ×4 of the stat's usual value); you can also type the exact number.
forgeguide_order_3_body: How far the stat counts. With the lock open, anything above the cap just stops counting; with it closed, any piece above the cap is discarded. Empty (∞) = no cap.
forgeguide_order_4_body: Power counts toward Strength, Intelligence, Chance and Agility. Characteristic points are not set by hand: The Forger spends them on its own for every combination it tries, item conditions first.
forgeguide_order_example: AP ≥ 11 with a cap of 12 and the lock closed (never 13 wasted AP), MP ≥ 6, Strength with no minimum and high purity: The Forger secures the AP and MP, then packs in as much Strength as it can.
forgeguide_intensity_intro: How long it runs and how many of your CPU cores it uses. Everything runs in your browser: nothing is sent to a server.
forgeguide_intensity_1_body: To try ideas and tune the order.
forgeguide_intensity_2_body: The recommended one. Uses half your CPU and tempers itself once it settles.
forgeguide_intensity_3_body: Your whole CPU, for orders with many minimums at once.
forgeguide_intensity_4_body: Never goes out on its own: it searches until you temper it.
forgeguide_items_intro: Want a build around one specific weapon, or never to be offered a certain item? That is what the Items section of the order is for. Pin and ban as many as you like.
forgeguide_items_1_body: Before starting, The Forger puts each pinned item in its slot and only searches the others around it, so pinning never slows it down: it narrows the search. If the item belongs to a set, completing that set is tried first. And unlike a kept slot, a pinned item still gets runes.
forgeguide_items_2_body: Search it by name (or by its set's name) in the Items section and tap Pin — or press Enter; tap your current gear in the "From the planner" row; or use the 📌 that shows when hovering an equipped planner slot or an item of a result.
forgeguide_items_3_body: Each pinned item shows its slot. Rings and Dofus share slots (two rings, six Dofus/trophies) and a Prysmaradite always takes the first one. If something does not fit — a third ring, a second Prysmaradite, a slot you keep — it turns red and the forge won't light until you fix it. If the item is above your character's level, you get a warning.
forgeguide_items_4_body: For items you don't own, don't want to farm or just don't like. Ban from the search or with the ⛔ on an item of a result, then forge again. An item can't be pinned and banned at the same time.
forgeguide_items_5_body: Pinned and banned items stay saved in this browser for your next forges. "Clear" empties each list.
forgeguide_items_example: You want an Earth build with one specific wand: search it, pin it, set your minimums and light the forge. Every result wears it; ban the ring you don't own too and none of them uses it.
forgeguide_slots_intro: Another way to keep something still, different from pinning.
forgeguide_slots_1_title: Unticking a slot = keeping it as is
forgeguide_slots_1_body: The slot stays exactly as it is in the planner: the same item (or empty) and the same runes you gave it. Handy for an item you already forgemaged and won't touch.
forgeguide_slots_2_body: Pin when you want the item and let The Forger decide its runes (and, for a ring or Dofus, which slot). Keep when you want that slot frozen, runes included. Slots a pinned item will take are marked with 📌.
forgeguide_forgemagic_intro: The Forger also picks one rune per item, as you would in the game.
forgeguide_forgemagic_1_body: One official rune (Tra/Pa/Ra) per forgeable item, sized by the line the item already has. Turn it off for gear without forgemagic.
forgeguide_forgemagic_2_body: Only added where they complete a missing minimum, never "just in case". Choose which ones are allowed, the maximum per build and whether they go on rings only.
forgeguide_forgemagic_3_body: Calculates as if every characteristic already had its scroll (+100). Turn it off to use the scrolls ticked on your sheet.
forgeguide_forgemagic_4_body: Limits the items' level, for example for a transition build. It never goes above your character's level.
forgeguide_forging_intro: The forge screen shows the best piece found so far, live, and which minimums it already meets.
forgeguide_forging_1_body: Drops as the piece stops improving. Once it cools down completely (with every minimum met) it tempers itself.
forgeguide_forging_2_body: If it looks stuck, the bellows melt fresh metal to search somewhere else, without losing the best piece.
forgeguide_forging_3_body: Finish now: it does one last item-by-item polish and shows the results.
forgeguide_forging_4_body: Cancels and goes back to the order with no results.
forgeguide_results_intro: Once tempered you get the best piece and up to four truly different alternatives.
forgeguide_results_1_body: "Masterpiece" = meets every minimum. Quality is negative while something is missing (how much purity is lost) and positive once everything is met (how much purity is left over): use it to compare pieces of the same order.
forgeguide_results_2_body: What the piece has beyond each minimum. That is your margin: if there is plenty of something, raise that minimum or ask for another stat.
forgeguide_results_3_title: Reforge, From scratch and Adjust order
forgeguide_results_3_body: Reforge relights the forge starting from these pieces (the result never gets worse). From scratch searches again from nothing. Adjust order goes back to the settings.
forgeguide_results_4_title: Pin or ban from a result
forgeguide_results_4_body: Hover an item: 📌 pins it and ⛔ bans it for the next forge. That is how you iterate: like the weapon, pin it; don't own that ring, ban it; then reforge.
forgeguide_results_5_body: Sends it to the planner: items, runes, exos, points and scrolls. Kept slots don't change.
forgeguide_faq_intro: What people ask most about The Forger.
forgeguide_faq_1_title: It doesn't meet all my minimums, what now?
forgeguide_faq_1_body: Try the Master forge, lower the hardest minimum a little, remove locked caps or unban items. Sometimes the order is impossible with the gear that exists: the checklist shows which minimum is missing and by how much.
forgeguide_faq_2_title: Why does each forge give something different?
forgeguide_faq_2_body: It is an evolutionary search with randomness: very open orders have many almost equally good pieces. Pin what you liked and reforge to refine around it.
forgeguide_faq_3_title: Does pinning many items slow it down?
forgeguide_faq_3_body: No, the opposite: every pinned item is one fewer slot to search.
forgeguide_faq_4_title: Does it account for Dofus and legendary passives?
forgeguide_faq_4_body: Yes, if you tick "Count item passives" in the order: at their best (full stacks, first case or turn 1) or as you set them in the planner. They come in sections (Dofus, Prysmaradites, legendary items): switch a whole section off or, with ⚙, only the passives that make no sense for how you play, such as AP per enemy finished off. Results mark it with ⚔, and loading the build sets the same passives for the "In combat" view. Final damage and vulnerability aren't order stats, so they don't change the choice.
forgeguide_faq_5_body: Yes, in this browser: stats, intensity, forgemagic, slots, pinned and banned items are still there next time you open The Forger.

dmgguide_seo_title: How Dofus Damage Works: the real formula | Dofus Forge
dmgguide_seo_description: Dofus 3's real damage formula, explained step by step with numeric examples: characteristic, Power, flat damage, % damage, critical, resistance and push damage.
dmgguide_intro: Dofus damage isn't just "more characteristic = more damage". This guide walks through the real formula, step by step, with concrete numbers, so you understand why the Forger prioritizes what it prioritizes.
dmgguide_order_intro: A hit's damage is worked out in this exact order. Change the order and the result changes, so the big picture first.
dmgguide_order_1_title: 1. The spell or weapon's base roll
dmgguide_order_1_body: Every spell or weapon has a base damage range (e.g. 80 to 100) before your character adds anything. That roll is the starting point for everything below.
dmgguide_order_2_body: Strength, Intelligence, Chance or Agility (whichever matches the hit's element) plus Power are added together and applied as a % on top of the base roll. They are not added straight to the damage.
dmgguide_order_3_body: Damage, elemental Damage and best-element Damage are added once already scaled, as flat points. They aren't multiplied by the characteristic.
dmgguide_order_4_body: % Melee/Ranged Damage, then % Spell/Weapon Damage, then % Final Damage and % Damage taken by the target. Each one multiplies the previous result.
dmgguide_order_5_title: 5. The target's resistance is subtracted last
dmgguide_order_5_body: Flat resistance first, then % resistance on what's left. The result never drops below 0.
dmgguide_mastery_intro: This happens before any percentage: it's the base everything else multiplies.
dmgguide_mastery_1_title: One characteristic point = 1% of the base roll
dmgguide_mastery_1_body: Strength, Intelligence, Chance or Agility don't add flat damage: they add a % on top of the base roll of the hit. That's why 10 points don't always equal "1 damage": they're worth more on a spell with a high roll and less on one with a low roll.
dmgguide_mastery_2_title: Power works the exact same way, point for point
dmgguide_mastery_2_body: Power is added to the characteristic before the % is applied, so it's worth exactly as much as one point of the characteristic matching the hit's element.
dmgguide_mastery_3_title: Flat damage is added after, not before
dmgguide_mastery_3_body: Damage, elemental Damage and best-element Damage are added as flat points on top of the already-scaled hit. The characteristic/Power scaling doesn't touch them, but the % multipliers that come next do.
dmgguide_mastery_example: With a base roll of 100: 300 Strength + 50 Power scale the hit to 450, and +50 flat Earth Damage bring it to 500, before any % is applied.
dmgguide_percent_intro: Everything above (scaled hit + flat damage) is multiplied by these four, in this order. They multiply each other, they don't add up.
dmgguide_percent_1_body: Depending on whether the hit was melee or ranged: the first of the four to apply.
dmgguide_percent_2_body: Depending on whether it was a spell or a weapon hit: applied right after the previous one.
dmgguide_percent_3_body: Only combat passives grant this (Dofus, legendaries), never a regular gear stat.
dmgguide_percent_4_body: The target's own vulnerability (e.g. Scissors of Destiny, Thanatena): the last multiplier before resistance.
dmgguide_percent_example: With 500 already-scaled damage: +10% Melee Damage brings it to 550, and +15% Spell Damage on top of that brings it to 632, not 625, as a flat 10%+15%=25% would.
dmgguide_critical_intro: A lot of people assume a critical hit multiplies the final damage. It doesn't.
dmgguide_critical_1_title: % Critical decides whether the hit crits
dmgguide_critical_1_body: It's a chance, not a multiplier: if it doesn't trigger, the hit is just the normal one.
dmgguide_critical_2_title: Critical Damage is added as extra flat damage
dmgguide_critical_2_body: On a crit, Critical Damage is added alongside the rest of the flat damage, before the % multipliers, exactly like elemental Damage. That's why a crit hits much harder with good % damage stacked than without them.
dmgguide_resistance_intro: The target's resistance acts last, in two steps, never earlier.
dmgguide_resistance_1_body: Subtracted straight from the already-computed damage, in flat points.
dmgguide_resistance_2_body: The % doesn't apply to the total damage, only to what remains after flat resistance is subtracted, and the result is rounded down.
dmgguide_resistance_3_body: (This is the exact same formula the site's PvP arena uses.) Very high resistance can block a hit entirely, but it never turns it into healing.
dmgguide_resistance_example: With 632 damage: 50 flat resistance brings it down to 582, and 20% resistance on that leaves 465.
dmgguide_push_intro: When a spell pushes the target back, every forced cell of displacement deals damage of its own, separate from the hit itself.
dmgguide_push_1_body: Raises the damage dealt per cell of knockback. It's an independent mechanic from the hit's elemental damage.
dmgguide_push_2_body: Reduces that push damage on the target's side. For now this guide covers it at the game-mechanic level: the Forger doesn't yet simulate full fights against a target (see the roadmap's damage mode).
dmgguide_example_title: A full example, number by number
dmgguide_example_intro: The same calculation above, start to finish, with a normal hit and a critical one.
dmgguide_example_scenario: An Earth hit with a 100 base roll, 300 Strength, 50 Power and +50 flat Earth Damage, with +10% Melee Damage and +15% Spell Damage, against a target with 50 flat Earth resistance and 20% Earth resistance.
dmgguide_example_crit_label: On a critical hit (+80 Critical Damage)
dmgguide_example_crit_body: The same hit, critical: {{normal}} damage becomes {{crit}}, because Critical Damage was added as flat damage before the %s, just like the rest.
dmgguide_faq_intro: The most common questions about how damage is split up.
dmgguide_faq_1_title: Do 10 characteristic points always mean the same damage?
dmgguide_faq_1_body: No. They're worth 1% of THAT spell or weapon hit's base roll. On one with a high roll they're worth more than on one with a low roll.
dmgguide_faq_2_title: Which matters more, the characteristic or % Spell Damage?
dmgguide_faq_2_body: It depends on the build, but % Spell Damage multiplies EVERYTHING before it (characteristic, Power and flat damage together), while the characteristic only scales the base roll. That's usually why it's worth more once the rest of your damage is already high.
dmgguide_faq_3_title: Does a crit apply an extra % on top of the hit?
dmgguide_faq_3_body: No. Critical Damage is added as flat damage before the % multipliers, not as a separate multiplier. That's why a crit hits harder the better your % damage stats are, not by a fixed amount.
dmgguide_faq_4_title: Why doesn't my build gain the same damage on every spell?
dmgguide_faq_4_body: Because the characteristic and Power scale each spell or weapon's own BASE roll. One with a high roll gains more flat damage per mastery point than one with a low roll, even though the % multipliers apply equally to both.
dmgguide_formula_note: The ⌊ ⌋ brackets round down to the nearest whole number, at the exact two points where the game itself rounds. This is Dofus 3's real formula, the same one the Forger uses internally.
